--- title: "[EventTime]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A vector of event times that may be exact, or right-, left-, or interval-censored. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_event_time.py#L226-L494){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python EventTime(*, time, time_max, paired, status) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `EventTime` is the Python counterpart of etd's `event_time` vector. Create one with `event_time()`, which validates its input, or with `new_event_time()`, which only checks types. Direct instantiation is for internal use. Each element has a time and a single-letter status: `"e"` (exact event), `"r"` (right-censored), `"l"` (left-censored), or `"i"` (interval-censored, with an upper bound in `time_max`). Elements print the way etd prints them: `7` for an event, `5+` for right censoring, `3-` for left censoring, and `[2, 4]` for an interval. The vector supports `len()`, indexing with an integer, a slice, an integer array, or a boolean mask (always returning an `EventTime`), and `EventTime.concat()` to combine vectors. Use `extract_time()` and `extract_status()` to get the components back, and `~~greenwood.EventTime.to_frame()` for a table with `time`, `status`{.gd-no-link}, and `time_max` columns. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#c72ddd84 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw x = gw.event_time( time=[7, 5, 3, 2, None], status=["e", "r", "l", "i", None], time_max=[None, None, None, 4, None], ) x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 7 5+ 3- [2, 4] ``` ::: ::: Indexing returns another `EventTime`: ::: {#f8a69900 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} x[1:4] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 5+ 3- [2, 4] ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
concat() Combine event-time vectors end to end, as `c()` does in R.
format() Format each element as etd does, with `None` for missing elements.
is_na() Return which elements are missing.
to_frame() Split the vector into a table with `time`, `status`{.gd-no-link}, and `time_max` columns.
### [concat()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Combine event-time vectors end to end, as `c()` does in R. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_event_time.py#L326-L366){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python concat(items) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [items]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Iterable[EventTime]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The `EventTime` vectors to combine, in order. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [EventTime]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A vector holding every element of `items`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#34a1ce18 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw a = gw.event_time(time=[7, 5], status=["e", "r"]) b = gw.event_time(time=[1], status=["i"], time_max=[3]) gw.EventTime.concat([a, b]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 7 5+ [1, 3] ``` ::: ::: ### [format()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Format each element as etd does, with `None` for missing elements. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_event_time.py#L392-L435){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python format() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Every number in the vector is formatted together, with R's rules: at most 7 significant digits, a shared number of decimal places, and scientific notation when it is narrower. Events get a trailing space, right-censored values a `+`, left-censored values a `-`, and intervals are written as `[lower, upper]`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list of str or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One string per element, or `None` where the element is missing. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#e6addf74 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw x = gw.event_time(time=[7, 5.5, 3], status=["e", "r", "i"], time_max=[None, None, 4]) x.format() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['7.0 ', '5.5+', '[3.0, 4.0]'] ``` ::: ::: ### [is_na()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return which elements are missing. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_event_time.py#L370-L390){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python is_na() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} An element is missing when any of its times is missing (`nan`), matching etd's `is.na()`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A boolean array, one entry per element. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#1c081ece .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw x = gw.event_time(time=[7, None, 2], status=["e", None, "i"], time_max=[None, None, 4]) x.is_na() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` array([False, True, False]) ``` ::: ::: ### [to_frame()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Split the vector into a table with `time`, `status`{.gd-no-link}, and `time_max` columns. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_event_time.py#L457-L494){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python to_frame(*, format=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is the counterpart of etd's `as_tibble()`. `time_max` is always included, and is missing for elements that aren't interval-censored. Missing values are nulls. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. When `None`, a backend is auto-detected (Polars, then Pandas, then PyArrow). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pandas.DataFrame, polars.DataFrame, or pyarrow.Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One row per element. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#f3c118a5 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw x = gw.event_time(time=[7, 5, 2], status=["e", "r", "i"], time_max=[None, None, 4]) x.to_frame(format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
